verdict.rationale: monday.com documents its own natural-language surfaces. Users can message or @mention agents to start work, describe a workflow in their own words to create an agent, and use monday vibe to turn words into work apps. External AI clients can also operate it through the hosted MCP. The evidence is all vendor marketing and does not show how much of the product can be driven by natural language, so coverage is partial. Missing for 10: documentation that general product operations (creating and editing boards, items and columns, configuring settings) can be done through natural-language commands, and independent or hands-on corroboration of how reliable the natural-language control is.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Talk to agents like teammates. Message them in updates, assign them items, and @mention them in any conversation to kick off real work — replies, statuses, and follow-ups included.
Describe any workflow in your own words to create a unique agent in minutes.
Before coding, try turning words into work apps using monday vibe.
Work with tools like Claude, Copilot, and ChatGPT through official integrations or the monday MCP
Use our native integration, or manually connect with our hosted MCP url.
